title: Kornati with Kids: Family Apartments & Activities 2027
metaDescription: Where to stay and what to do with children near Kornati, Croatia: Murter apartments, boat trips, beaches, park ticket costs and practical tips.
content:
## Where Should a Family Stay for Kornati?

The best base is the island of Murter, not the Kornati islands themselves. The national park covers 89 islands, islets and reefs, and its only permanent settlement is the small cluster of houses in Vrulje bay on Kornat. Shops, pharmacies, a doctor and ferries-to-mainland services are all on Murter. A bridge links Murter to the mainland, so a car works for the whole stay.

One local agency alone lists more than 300 apartments on Murter, so supply is not the problem. Choosing the right village is.

### Murter Town and Slanica Beach

Murter is the largest settlement and the most practical choice. The centre has supermarkets, a farmers' market, restaurants and the main harbour where most Kornati excursion boats depart. Slanica beach lies about 2 km from the centre. It is the best-known beach on the island and has shallow water, which suits toddlers and non-swimmers. Apartments for 4+1 or 6+2 people near Slanica are common. Look for air conditioning, a washing machine and a terrace, since you will rinse a lot of salty swimwear.

### Jezera

Jezera is quieter and works for families with children under 6. The pace is slow, and Kornati excursions also depart from here. Evening options are limited to a few konobas and ice cream stands.

### Betina

Betina is a small harbour village with a traditional shipbuilding history. Its Museum of Wooden Shipbuilding is a short, easy stop for school-age children. The village is compact, so children can walk safely along the waterfront.

### Kornati Fisherman Houses

Some owners rent simple fisherman houses on the islands, reachable only by boat. The setting is remote and the nights are very dark. This idea works well in photos, but with children under 8 it is the wrong choice. There are no shops, no nearby doctor and limited power and water, and a stomach bug turns into a boat evacuation. Book one only for a night or two with older kids who swim confidently.

## How Much Do Kornati Tours Cost for Families?

Tour prices change by season and operator. Typical figures:

- **Large excursion boats from Murter:** around €35–60 per adult. One Murter operator charges €60 for adults and €30 for ages 5–12, with children up to 5 free. The price includes the park ticket, guide, welcome drink and lunch.
- **Tours from Zadar, Biograd or Vodice:** roughly €60–80 per adult, with longer transfers.
- **Speedboat with a skipper (1–6 people):** priced per boat and tailored to your timing. It suits families who want to avoid a crowd of 60–150 people.
- **Own boat:** the park ticket is charged per boat, not per person. A small private boat up to 6.99 m pays about €25 in low season and €45 in high season when bought in advance. The same ticket bought from a ranger boat inside the park costs about double.

Buy tickets online or at an agency before sailing. Tickets for a boat day cannot be bought at any gate, because the park has none.

## Best Activities for Kids in and Around Kornati

### Boat Day Through the Archipelago

Boats leave Murter's main harbour at about 09:00 and return by 18:00. The route passes the cliffs on the open-sea side, stops for swimming at bays such as Modri bok on Kornat, and often includes Levrnaka island with a short walk to a viewpoint. Lunch is served on board or in a konoba. Children aged 6 and up cope well with the nine hours. For younger ones, a speedboat or half-day trip is easier.

### Snorkelling

Surface snorkelling is allowed and needs no permit across the park, except in the four strict-protection zones where swimming is banned. The best water is from June to September, with sea temperatures of 20–27°C. June and September have the same clarity as July with fewer boats. Bring child-sized masks, since many boats carry only adult sizes.

### Cliff Jumping and Swimming Stops

Some boats, including operators out of Zadar, offer cliff jumping and snorkelling stops. Most boat stops use a ladder from the deck. Children who cannot swim should wear a vest at every stop.

### Beach Days on Murter

Slanica is the main option for shallow water. For something quieter, ask your host for a small cove near Betina or Jezera. Many local agencies also rent kayaks and SUP boards, which works well for children over 8 in calm morning conditions.

### Telašćica Nature Park

Some boat tours combine Kornati with Telašćica and its salt lake Mir. The lake is saltier and warmer than the sea, and children usually enjoy swimming in it. Tours from Biograd and Zadar often include this stop.

## Local Tips for Families

- **Pick a boat by size.** A 150-passenger boat means queues at lunch. A wooden sailboat for 40–55 people feels calmer.
- **Go in June or September.** Sea temperatures are comfortable, boats are fewer and apartment prices fall by about 20–30% against July and August.
- **Pack shade.** Most islands have little tree cover. Bring hats, UV swimsuits and a sunshade for the beach.
- **Bring water and snacks.** Lunch is fixed-menu on most tours, and picky eaters should have their own food. Ask for a vegetarian menu when booking.
- **Check the weather.** Strong bora or sirocco winds cancel trips. Keep one spare day in your schedule.
- **Ask for a cot or high chair** at booking. Many apartments supply one free or for a small fee.

## When to Visit

The park is open year-round, but family trips work best from May to September. Swimming is comfortable from June. July and August are hot, busy and expensive, and timed-entry slots can sell out, so book ahead.

faq.question: Can you stay overnight in Kornati National Park with kids?
faq.answer: Yes, but only in a few simple fisherman houses and konoba rooms on the islands, reachable by boat. There are no hotels or shops. Families with young children are better off staying on Murter and making a day trip.

faq.question: What is the best base for a family trip to Kornati?
faq.answer: Murter town is the most practical, with supermarkets, restaurants, the main excursion harbour and shallow Slanica beach about 2 km away. Jezera and Betina are quieter alternatives. All three are on Murter island and connected by road.

faq.question: How much does a Kornati boat trip cost for a family of four?
faq.answer: On a large boat from Murter, two adults and two children aged 5–12 pay roughly €150–200 in total, depending on the operator and season. Children under 5 usually go free. The price typically includes the park ticket, guide and lunch.

faq.question: Is Kornati suitable for toddlers?
faq.answer: A full-day trip is demanding for children under 4, with up to nine hours on a boat in strong sun and no shade on most islands. A short speedboat trip or a beach day at Slanica is easier. Life vests and sun protection are essential.

faq.question: Do children pay for the Kornati National Park ticket?
faq.answer: On organised tours the ticket is bundled into the price, and children get discounted or free places depending on age (often free under 5). On your own boat, the ticket is charged per boat, not per person, starting around €25 in advance.

faq.question: When is the best time to visit Kornati with children?
faq.answer: June and September offer sea temperatures of 20–27°C, clear water and fewer boats than July and August. Apartment prices are also lower. Avoid the middle of August if your children dislike crowds.

quickAnswer: Kornati National Park has no hotels or towns, so families stay in apartments on Murter island (Murter, Betina, Jezera) and visit the park by boat. Full-day tours cost roughly €35–80, usually include the park ticket and lunch, and run from about 09:00 to 18:00. Children under 5 often travel free.
